Naomi — assigning the artifacts below. See inline answers + attached artifacts (redwood_sbom_summary.csv, pen_test_summary_q1_2026.pdf, config-ops-patch-policy-2026.pdf). I kept language procurement-friendly.

Summary answers (for the RFI):

1) SAST / DAST:
- SAST: Static analysis runs on every PR via our CI pipeline (pre-merge). Full repository scans are scheduled weekly across all managed services. We use a combination of open-source SAST (semgrep/custom rules) and commercial scanners; findings are triaged into our ticketing system with severity labels and assigned SLAs.
- DAST: Dynamic scans are performed monthly against production endpoints and on-demand for release candidates (pre-GA). DAST results are correlated with runtime logs to reduce false positives.

2) Penetration testing:
- External full-scope penetration tests are conducted annually (third-party testers). For Q1 2026 we performed a targeted external assessment focused on our serving runtime and orchestration control plane — executive summary attached (pen_test_summary_q1_2026.pdf). Redacted vulnerability details have been removed; we can provide a signed NDA copy with fuller findings if required.

3) Patch SLAs and remediation windows (operational commitment):
- Critical (active exploit or RCE): initial mitigation/rollback within 24 hours, patch/hotfix deployed within 72 hours and communicated to affected customers.
- High (privilege escalation / high impact): mitigation plan within 48 hours, patch deployed within 7 calendar days.
- Medium: fix planned and scheduled within 30 calendar days.
- Low: tracked in backlog and reviewed each release cycle.
Notes: SLA timing refers to Redwoods operational remediation timeline; customers may require additional coordination for private deployments. We maintain change logs and remediation evidence for audits.

4) SBOM coverage and formats:
- We generate SBOMs for all published container images and language-level artifacts we ship. Coverage includes first-order and transitive dependencies for managed images/bundles.
- Output formats supported: SPDX (preferred) and CycloneDX; we also export CSV summaries for procurement/audit consumption (sample attached: redwood_sbom_summary.csv).
- We can produce per-release SBOM bundles and attest signatures where required.

5) CVE tracking and customer integrations:
- Centralized CVE ingestion pipeline that maps vendor advisories to internal package manifests. Findings generate tickets automatically in our internal tracker and are surfaced to customer-facing incident dashboards for Dedicated/Private customers.
- We offer webhook integrations to push CVE notices to customer systems (Jira, ServiceNow) on request and keep an audit timeline for each CVE.

6) Evidence and attestation:
- We can provide a redacted pen test executive summary (attached), SBOM exports, and an attestation letter confirming patching practices and scan cadence. For full pen test reports or vulnerability artifacts, we require an NDA and a short request process.

Attachments included for Holdings RFI: redwood_sbom_summary.csv, pen_test_summary_q1_2026.pdf, config-ops-patch-policy-2026.pdf

If you want, I can turn this into a 1-page procurement-ready response document. Ben, can you add a short blurb about how we handle emergency hotfix communications for Dedicated customers?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
